macro_blurb: Geopolitics remain front and center as traders push back on Iran's timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, while President Trump signaled that rising economic costs will not pressure him into an Iran deal, and Norway moved under France's nuclear umbrella in a notable European defense realignment. In US tech, Snowflake jumped 36% after an earnings beat paired with a $6 billion Amazon cloud commitment, while Salesforce posted another AI-driven record result but offered a softer outlook, prompting CEO Marc Benioff to lay out a turnaround plan. On the regulatory front, the White House is weighing a CFTC proposal on prediction-market rules, and a UK report warned that one in six young people risk being out of work or training within five years absent intervention.
synthesis:
Today's screen is a momentum-and-value tape with a US-only footprint: all 10 picks are American, average momentum percentile sits at 90.7 and value at 79.1, while quality lags at 60.3. Healthcare contributes 3 of 10 names, Consumer Cyclical 2, and no single sector dominates beyond that — but the composite range is tight (73.0 to 84.3), so the screen is telling us conviction is broad rather than concentrated. Notably, of 992 tickers screened and 163 scored, Technology and Financial Services produced zero top-10 entrants. That is the headline.

The Healthcare trio — CNC, BIIB, DVA — shares a clear thread: deep value paired with extreme momentum, masking quality stress. Centene's 23.6% FCF yield and +31.9% three-month return sit against a -26% ROE; DaVita's 81% ROE is a debt/equity-1,261 artifact; Biogen's cheapness coexists with pipeline setbacks. This is a "left-for-dead bounce" cohort, not a quality cohort. Separately, APA and DAL ride the same macro pulse from opposite sides — APA (+15.6%, P/E 8.5x) leveraged to the Hormuz risk premium, DAL (+27.3%, P/E 11.9x) leveraged to softer crude. One trade hedges the other.

The outlier is DECK: 90th-percentile Quality, debt/equity of 15, but only modest momentum and no yield — it doesn't fit the cheap-and-running template. The conspicuous absence is Technology, against a tape where Snowflake just printed +36%; the screen is plainly not chasing it. Watch two things over the next fortnight: any Hormuz de-escalation (it unwinds APA and re-rates DAL) and the Iran-deal posture Trump has now publicly hardened against.
